content: Entire is enabled for this repo. Run `entire agent-help` to see what entire does and which subcommand to use, then `entire agent-help <command>` for that command's exact, current flags. Commits automatically capture the AI session as a checkpoint, so never create checkpoints by hand — just commit normally. Before large edits, `entire why <file>:<line>` and `entire checkpoint search` recover the intent behind existing code. Leave setup and destructive commands (enable, disable, clean, rewind, auth) to the user. This repo is auto-detected from the git origin remote as gh/entireio/cli; you are already inside it, so never ask the user for the repo name.

arguments.command: entire agent-help && printf '\n--- configure ---\n' && entire agent-help configure
git status --short && git branch --show-current && git log -5 --oneline

Entire's CLI is the source of truth for its own usage. Do not guess flags or
subcommands — read them from this command. You are already inside the repo:
entire auto-detects it from the git origin remote, so never ask the user for the
repo name. Pass --repo only to target a DIFFERENT repo.

Current repo: gh/entireio/cli  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

When to use entire:
  activity     Show your activity overview
  agent        Manage agent integrations (add, remove, list)
  api          Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
  auth         Manage authentication
  blame        Show which lines came from Entire checkpoints
  checkpoint   Inspect and search checkpoints
  clean        Clean up Entire session data
  configure    Update Entire settings in the current repository
  disable      Disable Entire in current repository
  dispatch     Generate a dispatch summarizing recent agent work
  doctor       Diagnose and fix session issues
  enable       Enable Entire in current repository
  experts      Rank agent provenance for code scopes
  grant        Manage Entire access grants and org membership
  import       Import pre-existing agent history into Entire (experimental)
  investigate  Run a multi-agent investigation against the current branch
  labs         Explore experimental Entire workflows
  login        Log in to Entire
  logout       Log out of Entire
  org          Manage Entire organizations
  plugin       Manage Entire plugins (install, list, upgrade, search, remove)
  project      Manage Entire projects
  recap        Summarize recent checkpoint activity
  repo         Manage Entire repositories
  review       Run a multi-agent review against the current branch
  runner       Set up and tune trail runners for this repository
  search       Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
  session      Manage agent sessions tracked by Entire
  status       Show Entire status
  tokens       Analyze token usage across sessions and checkpoints
  trail        Manage trails for your branches
  version      Show build information
  why          Show why a line exists

Drill in for exact, currently-installed flags:  entire agent-help <command>  (e.g. entire agent-help trail)
Add --json for structured output.

--- configure ---
entire configure — Update Entire settings in the current repository
Update non-agent Entire settings in the current repository.

Manages telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy options, and summary
provider configuration. Agent installation is handled by 'entire agent'.

Examples:
  entire configure                                # Show this help
  entire configure --telemetry=false              # Opt out of telemetry
  entire configure --absolute-git-hook-path       # Reinstall git hook with absolute path
  entire configure --force                        # Reinstall git hook
  entire configure --checkpoint-remote github:org/checkpoints
  entire configure --checkpoint-backend refs      # Store each checkpoint as its own git ref
  entire configure --summarize-provider claude-code
  entire configure --summarize-timeout-seconds 300   # 5m deadline for explain --generate

Current repo: gh/entireio/cli  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path          Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --checkpoint-backend string       Checkpoint storage backend: refs (one git ref per checkpoint; recommended) or branch (shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-remote string        Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                           Reinstall the Entire git hook
      --local                           Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --project                         Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --skip-push-sessions              Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --summarize-model string          Set the model hint used by explain --generate
      --summarize-provider string       Set the provider used by explain --generate (e.g., claude-code, codex, gemini, pi, cursor, copilot-cli)
      --summarize-timeout-seconds int   Set the hard deadline (seconds) for explain --generate summary generation. 0 clears (falls back to 5m default).
      --telemetry                       Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)

content.text:
Interactively connect the current repository to Entire, choose a mirror,
select agent integrations, and save the resulting configuration.

When flags are supplied, configure remains a non-interactive settings editor for
telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy options, and summary providers.

Examples:
  entire configure                                # Run interactive onboarding
  entire configure --telemetry=false              # Opt out of telemetry
  entire configure --absolute-git-hook-path       # Reinstall git hook with absolute path
  entire configure --force                        # Reinstall git hook
  entire configure --checkpoint-remote github:org/checkpoints
  entire configure --checkpoint-backend refs      # Store each checkpoint as its own git ref
  entire configure --summarize-provider claude-code
  entire configure --summarize-timeout-seconds 300   # 5m deadline for explain --generate

Usage:
  entire configure [flags]

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path          Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --checkpoint-backend string       Checkpoint storage backend: refs (one git ref per checkpoint; recommended) or branch (shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-remote string        Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                           Reinstall the Entire git hook
  -h, --help                            help for configure
      --local                           Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --project                         Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --skip-push-sessions              Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --summarize-model string          Set the model hint used by explain --generate
      --summarize-provider string       Set the provider used by explain --generate (e.g., claude-code, codex, gemini, pi, cursor, copilot-cli)
      --summarize-timeout-seconds int   Set the hard deadline (seconds) for explain --generate summary generation. 0 clears (falls back to 5m default).
      --telemetry                       Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)

Interactive onboarding requires a terminal. For agent-only setup, use 'entire agent'.

content.text:
Implemented the interactive `entire configure` onboarding flow.

### Highlights
- Login/re-authentication when no valid session exists.
- GitHub App access detection with admin/non-admin guidance and installation polling.
- Region selection and mirror creation.
- Upstream mirror selection and local remote configuration.
- Unified agent multi-select and hook setup.
- Save flow supporting direct push or a new review branch, including protected-branch detection.
- Automatic configuration commit/push on clean worktrees; safely skips commits when pre-existing changes exist.
- Existing flag-based `configure` behavior remains non-interactive.

### Files
- `cmd/entire/cli/configure_onboarding.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/configure_onboarding_test.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go`

### Validation
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli -count=1` passes.
- `go vet ./cmd/entire/cli/...` passes.
- Lint only reports two pre-existing `goconst` findings in `plugin_fetch.go`.

I don't like the style of this:

┃ Which upstream do you want to use?
┃ > aws-ap-south-1 (in) — aws-ap-south-1.entire.io
┃   aws-ap-southeast-2 (au) — aws-ap-southeast-2.entire.io
┃   aws-eu-central-1 (eu) — aws-eu-central-1.entire.io
┃   aws-us-east-2 (us) — aws-us-east-2.entire.io

I want it to be like in my prototype instead. Also, after finishing this step, I want it to still be visible and accessible for the user! So they can go up and down because one doesn't depend on the other.

// Styles is a collection of styles for components of the form.
// Themes can be applied to a form using the WithTheme option.
type Styles struct {
	Form           FormStyles
	Group          GroupStyles
	FieldSeparator lipgloss.Style
	Blurred        FieldStyles
	Focused        FieldStyles
	Help           help.Styles
}

// FormStyles are the styles for a form.
type FormStyles struct {
	Base lipgloss.Style
}

// GroupStyles are the styles for a group.
type GroupStyles struct {
	Base        lipgloss.Style
	Title       lipgloss.Style
	Description lipgloss.Style
}

// FieldStyles are the styles for input fields.
type FieldStyles struct {
	Base           lipgloss.Style
	Title          lipgloss.Style
	Description    lipgloss.Style
	ErrorIndicator lipgloss.Style
	ErrorMessage   lipgloss.Style

	// Select styles.
	SelectSelector lipgloss.Style // Selection indicator
	Option         lipgloss.Style // Select options
	NextIndicator  lipgloss.Style
	PrevIndicator  lipgloss.Style

	// FilePicker styles.
	Directory lipgloss.Style
	File      lipgloss.Style

	// Multi-select styles.
	MultiSelectSelector lipgloss.Style
	SelectedOption      lipgloss.Style
	SelectedPrefix      lipgloss.Style
	UnselectedOption    lipgloss.Style
	UnselectedPrefix    lipgloss.Style

	// Textinput and teatarea styles.
	TextInput TextInputStyles

	// Confirm styles.
	FocusedButton lipgloss.Style
	BlurredButton lipgloss.Style

	// Card styles.
	Card      lipgloss.Style
	NoteTitle lipgloss.Style
	Next      lipgloss.Style
}

// TextInputStyles are the styles for text inputs.
type TextInputStyles struct {
	Cursor      lipgloss.Style
	CursorText  lipgloss.Style
	Placeholder lipgloss.Style
	Prompt      lipgloss.Style
	Text        lipgloss.Style
}

const (
	buttonPaddingHorizontal = 2
	buttonPaddingVertical   = 0
)

// ThemeBase returns a new base theme with general styles to be inherited by
// other themes.
func ThemeBase(bool) *Styles {
	var t Styles

	t.Form.Base = lipgloss.NewStyle()
	t.Group.Base = lipgloss.NewStyle()
	t.FieldSeparator = lipgloss.NewStyle().SetString("\n\n")

	button := lipgloss.NewStyle().
		Padding(buttonPaddingVertical, buttonPaddingHorizontal).
		MarginRight(1)

	// Focused styles.
	t.Focused.Base = lipgloss.NewStyle().PaddingLeft(1).BorderStyle(lipgloss.ThickBorder()).BorderLeft(true)
	t.Focused.Card = t.Focused.Base
	t.Focused.ErrorIndicator = lipgloss.NewStyle().SetString(" *")
	t.Focused.ErrorMessage = lipgloss.NewStyle().SetString(" *")
	t.Focused.SelectSelector = lipgloss.NewStyle().SetString("> ")
	t.Focused.NextIndicator = lipgloss.NewStyle().MarginLeft(1).SetString("→")
	t.Focused.PrevIndicator = lipgloss.NewStyle().MarginRight(1).SetString("←")
	t.Focused.MultiSelectSelector = lipgloss.NewStyle().SetString("> ")
	t.Focused.SelectedPrefix = lipgloss.NewStyle().SetString("[•] ")
	t.Focused.UnselectedPrefix = lipgloss.NewStyle().SetString("[ ] ")
	t.Focused.FocusedButton = button.Foreground(lipgloss.Color("0")).Background(lipgloss.Color("7"))
	t.Focused.BlurredButton = button.Foreground(lipgloss.Color("7")).Background(lipgloss.Color("0"))
	t.Focused.TextInput.Placeholder = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("8"))

	t.Help = help.New().Styles

	// Blurred styles.
	t.Blurred = t.Focused
	t.Blurred.Base = t.Blurred.Base.BorderStyle(lipgloss.HiddenBorder())
	t.Blurred.Card = t.Blurred.Base
	t.Blurred.MultiSelectSelector = lipgloss.NewStyle().SetString("  ")
	t.Blurred.NextIndicator = lipgloss.NewStyle()
	t.Blurred.PrevIndicator = lipgloss.NewStyle()

	return &t
}

// ThemeCharm returns a new theme based on the Charm color scheme.
func ThemeCharm(isDark bool) *Styles {
	t := ThemeBase(isDark)
	lightDark := lipgloss.LightDark(isDark)

	var (
		normalFg = lightDark(lipgloss.Color("252"), lipgloss.Color("235"))
		indigo   = lightDark(lipgloss.Color("#5A56E0"), lipgloss.Color("#7571F9"))
		cream    = lightDark(lipgloss.Color("#FFFDF5"), lipgloss.Color("#FFFDF5"))
		fuchsia  = lipgloss.Color("#F780E2")
		green    = lightDark(lipgloss.Color("#02BA84"), lipgloss.Color("#02BF87"))
		red      = lightDark(lipgloss.Color("#FF4672"), lipgloss.Color("#ED567A"))
	)

	t.Focused.Base = t.Focused.Base.BorderForeground(lipgloss.Color("238"))
	t.Focused.Card = t.Focused.Base
	t.Focused.Title = t.Focused.Title.Foreground(indigo).Bold(true)
	t.Focused.NoteTitle = t.Focused.NoteTitle.Foreground(indigo).Bold(true).MarginBottom(1)
	t.Focused.Directory = t.Focused.Directory.Foreground(indigo)
	t.Focused.Description = t.Focused.Description.Foreground(lightDark(lipgloss.Color(""), lipgloss.Color("243")))
	t.Focused.ErrorIndicator = t.Focused.ErrorIndicator.Foreground(red)
	t.Focused.ErrorMessage = t.Focused.ErrorMessage.Foreground(red)
	t.Focused.SelectSelector = t.Focused.SelectSelector.Foreground(fuchsia)
	t.Focused.NextIndicator = t.Focused.NextIndicator.Foreground(fuchsia)
	t.Focused.PrevIndicator = t.Focused.PrevIndicator.Foreground(fuchsia)
	t.Focused.Option = t.Focused.Option.Foreground(normalFg)
	t.Focused.MultiSelectSelector = t.Focused.MultiSelectSelector.Foreground(fuchsia)
	t.Focused.SelectedOption = t.Focused.SelectedOption.Foreground(green)
	t.Focused.SelectedPrefix = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lightDark(lipgloss.Color("#02CF92"), lipgloss.Color("#02A877"))).SetString("✓ ")
	t.Focused.UnselectedPrefix = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lightDark(lipgloss.Color(""), lipgloss.Color("243"))).SetString("• ")
	t.Focused.UnselectedOption = t.Focused.UnselectedOption.Foreground(normalFg)
	t.Focused.FocusedButton = t.Focused.FocusedButton.Foreground(cream).Background(fuchsia)

entire-config-debug: 1 windows (created Wed Aug 12 15:23:53 2026)
Interactively connect the current repository to Entire, choose a mirror,
select agent integrations, and save the resulting configuration.

When flags are supplied, configure remains a non-interactive settings editor for
telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy options, and summary providers.

Examples:
  entire configure                                # Run interactive onboarding
  entire configure --telemetry=false              # Opt out of telemetry
  entire configure --absolute-git-hook-path       # Reinstall git hook with absolute path
  entire configure --force                        # Reinstall git hook
  entire configure --checkpoint-remote github:org/checkpoints
  entire configure --checkpoint-backend refs      # Store each checkpoint as its own git ref
  entire configure --summarize-provider claude-code
  entire configure --summarize-timeout-seconds 300   # 5m deadline for explain --generate

Usage:
  entire configure [flags]

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path          Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --checkpoint-backend string       Checkpoint storage backend: refs (one git ref per checkpoint; recommended) or branch (shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-remote string        Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                           Reinstall the Entire git hook
  -h, --help                            help for configure
      --local                           Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --project                         Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --skip-push-sessions              Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --summarize-model string          Set the model hint used by explain --generate
      --summarize-provider string       Set the provider used by explain --generate (e.g., claude-code, codex, gemini, pi, cursor, copilot-cli)
      --summarize-timeout-seconds int   Set the hard deadline (seconds) for explain --generate summary generation. 0 clears (falls back to 5m default).
      --telemetry                       Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)

Interactive onboarding requires a terminal. For agent-only setup, use 'entire agent'.
EXIT:0

sleep 12
tmux capture-pane -p -e -t entire-config-debug -S -120

content.text: ok  	github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli	57.393s
(no output)

Found the actual issue: Enter was changing focus, but huh evaluated the dynamic title before applying the focus transition. The screen therefore looked unchanged until another keypress.

Fixed by forcing a redraw after every focus transition. Verified in a real tmux PTY:

- Enter immediately activates the agents section.
- Upstream `?` becomes muted.
- Agents `?` becomes orange.
- Shift+Tab immediately returns focus to upstream.
- Both sections remain visible.

Full CLI tests and vet pass.
Are we using charm?

Yes. The flow uses Charm libraries:

- `charm.land/huh/v2` for forms, select, and multi-select.
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` for keyboard events and focus transitions.
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` for styling and colors.

The custom wrappers around `huh.Select` and `huh.MultiSelect` provide the prototype-specific navigation and persistent two-section layout.

Problems:
1. I can arrow up/down across sections but this should only be possible per section and enter selects an option.
2. There is no "active" indication on the agents section, so it's not possible to see where the cursor currently is
3. There's no way to get passed this step, it's a dead end but there should be a save and submit step (see prototype)

Fixed the flow structurally:

1. **Arrow keys are section-local**
   - Upstream arrows wrap only among upstreams.
   - Agent arrows wrap only among agents.
   - Save arrows wrap only among save options.
   - Sections no longer change at list boundaries.

2. **Agent cursor is visible**
   - The focused agent row now has an orange `›`.
   - Checkboxes still independently show selected/unselected state.

3. **Added the missing save step**
   - `Enter` on upstream → agents.
   - `Enter` on agents → Save configuration.
   - `Enter` on Save submits and continues with configuration/commit/push.
   - `Shift+Tab` goes back one section.

I verified all three transitions in an actual tmux PTY, not only unit tests. Full CLI tests and vet pass.

summary:
## Goal
Implement a prototype-aligned interactive `entire configure` onboarding flow covering login, repository access, mirrors/upstream, agents, and save/push behavior. Keep upstream and agent choices visible and independently revisitable.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Bare `entire configure` should launch onboarding only in an interactive terminal; flag-based behavior remains non-interactive.
- Match the supplied HTML prototype’s visual style.
- Upstream labels should be region-only, e.g. `AU — your upstream`, `○ EU`, not cluster host details.
- Upstream and agent sections must remain visible together and support moving between them with arrow keys.
- Use consistent prototype indicators: green `●`/`◼`, muted `○`/`◻`, agent-colored dots, accented `?`, no `>` cursor or focused rail.
- Do not manually create checkpoints; normal commits capture them.
- Leave destructive/setup commands such as enable, disable, clean, rewind, and auth to the user.

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Added interactive onboarding in `cmd/entire/cli/configure_onboarding.go`.
- [x] Added login/session validation and GitHub App access handling, including admin/non-admin branches and installation polling.
- [x] Added region selection, mirror creation, upstream configuration, agent setup, and commit/push save flow.
- [x] Updated `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go` so bare interactive `configure` runs onboarding while flags retain existing behavior.
- [x] Added `EnableOptions.SuppressAdditionalSetup` to suppress unrelated Vercel/history prompts during onboarding.
- [x] Combined upstream and agent selection into one persistent form via `promptConfigureUpstreamAndAgents`.
- [x] Added custom styling through `newConfigureForm` and `configureFormTheme`.
- [x] Added boundary-based arrow navigation using `configureUpstreamField` and `configureAgentField`.
- [x] Fixed “stuck on upstream after pressing enter” by explicitly returning `huh.NextField` for Enter/Tab in `configureUpstreamField.Update`.
- [x] Added regression test `TestConfigureUpstreamFieldEnterAdvancesToAgents`.
- [x] Added tests for login, repository access, labels, ordering, styling, and generated-change isolation.
- [x] `go test ./cmd/entire/cli -count=1` and `go vet ./cmd/entire/cli/...` pass.

### In Progress
- [ ] User should manually verify the latest Enter/Tab transition and interactive navigation in a real terminal.

### Blocked
- `mise run lint:go` still fails only on two pre-existing `goconst` findings in `cmd/entire/cli/plugin_fetch.go` for `"https"` and `"http"`.

## Key Decisions
- **Single huh form/group**: Keeps upstream visible while agents are active and allows revisiting either independent choice.
- **Custom field wrappers**: `configureUpstreamField` and `configureAgentField` provide cross-section arrow navigation.
- **Explicit Enter/Tab transition**: Avoids huh field-position inference failing through the custom decorator.
- **Configure-specific theme installed first**: `newConfigureForm` uses `huh.NewForm(...).WithTheme(configureFormTheme())` because huh fields retain their first assigned theme.
- **Safe save behavior**: Commit automatically only on a clean worktree; preserve pre-existing user changes.

## Next Steps
1. Reproduce the interactive flow and confirm Enter advances from upstream to agents.
2. Verify Up/Down navigation crosses section boundaries and both sections remain visible.
3. Check the real terminal rendering against the prototype screenshots.
4. Run targeted/full tests after any UI adjustments.
5. Commit the changes normally when approved.

## Critical Context
- Modified/untracked files:
  - `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/configure_onboarding.go`
  - `cmd/entire/cli/configure_onboarding_test.go`
- Prototype comparison screenshots:
  - `/Users/dip/Library/Application Support/CleanShot/media/media_eSUmiqoczv/CleanShot 2026-08-12 at 14.57.26@2x.png`
  - `/Users/dip/Library/Application Support/CleanShot/media/media_6K9AeDqpLa/CleanShot 2026-08-12 at 14.58.35@2x.png`
- Latest fix is in `configureUpstreamField.Update`: Enter or Tab now returns `huh.NextField`.

content.text:
Use:

- **Radio lists:** arrows change selection; Enter confirms and proceeds.
- **Checkbox lists:** Space toggles the active checkbox; Enter confirms selections and proceeds.
- **Save:** arrows choose; Enter submits.
- **Shift+Tab:** returns to the previous section.

Enter should **not** behave like Space in a multi-select—otherwise there’s no clear primary action to finish the section. Tab can remain an alternate navigation key, but Enter semantically means “confirm and continue.”
Radio buttons are still changing indetation but should not!

2. Apply the configuration.

5. Skip the save prompt entirely when nothing changed or when pre-existing worktree changes prevent automatic commit/push.

package huh

import "charm.land/bubbles/v2/key"

// KeyMap is the keybindings to navigate the form.
type KeyMap struct {
	Quit key.Binding

	Confirm     ConfirmKeyMap
	FilePicker  FilePickerKeyMap
	Input       InputKeyMap
	MultiSelect MultiSelectKeyMap
	Note        NoteKeyMap
	Select      SelectKeyMap
	Text        TextKeyMap
}

// InputKeyMap is the keybindings for input fields.
type InputKeyMap struct {
	AcceptSuggestion key.Binding
	Next             key.Binding
	Prev             key.Binding
	Submit           key.Binding
}

// TextKeyMap is the keybindings for text fields.
type TextKeyMap struct {
	Next    key.Binding
	Prev    key.Binding
	NewLine key.Binding
	Editor  key.Binding
	Submit  key.Binding
}

// SelectKeyMap is the keybindings for select fields.
type SelectKeyMap struct {
	Next         key.Binding
	Prev         key.Binding
	Up           key.Binding
	Down         key.Binding
	HalfPageUp   key.Binding
	HalfPageDown key.Binding
	GotoTop      key.Binding
	GotoBottom   key.Binding
	Left         key.Binding
	Right        key.Binding
	Filter       key.Binding
	SetFilter    key.Binding
	ClearFilter  key.Binding
	Submit       key.Binding
}

// MultiSelectKeyMap is the keybindings for multi-select fields.
type MultiSelectKeyMap struct {
	Next         key.Binding
	Prev         key.Binding
	Up           key.Binding
	Down         key.Binding
	HalfPageUp   key.Binding
	HalfPageDown key.Binding
	GotoTop      key.Binding
	GotoBottom   key.Binding
	Toggle       key.Binding
	Filter       key.Binding
	SetFilter    key.Binding
	ClearFilter  key.Binding
	Submit       key.Binding
	SelectAll    key.Binding
	SelectNone   key.Binding
}

// FilePickerKeyMap is the keybindings for filepicker fields.
type FilePickerKeyMap struct {
	Open       key.Binding
	Close      key.Binding
	GotoTop    key.Binding
	GotoBottom key.Binding
	PageUp     key.Binding
	PageDown   key.Binding
	Back       key.Binding
	Select     key.Binding
	Up         key.Binding
	Down       key.Binding
	Prev       key.Binding
	Next       key.Binding
	Submit     key.Binding
}

// NoteKeyMap is the keybindings for note fields.
type NoteKeyMap struct {
	Next   key.Binding
	Prev   key.Binding
	Submit key.Binding
}

// ConfirmKeyMap is the keybindings for confirm fields.
type ConfirmKeyMap struct {
	Next   key.Binding
	Prev   key.Binding
	Toggle key.Binding
	Submit key.Binding
	Accept key.Binding
	Reject key.Binding
}

// NewDefaultKeyMap returns a new default keymap.
func NewDefaultKeyMap() *KeyMap {
	return &KeyMap{
		Quit: key.NewBinding(key.WithKeys("ctrl+c")),
		Input: InputKeyMap{
			AcceptSuggestion: key.NewBinding(key.WithKeys("ctrl+e"), key.WithHelp("ctrl+e", "complete")),

Setting `opts.Yes = true` here (to auto-answer choices already covered by the onboarding form) also silently short-circuits the telemetry consent prompt in `runEnableInteractive` (`setup.go`'s `if opts.Yes { ... } else if err := promptTelemetryConsent(...)`), which is not gated by the new `SuppressAdditionalSetup` flag the way the Vercel/history-import prompts are. As a result, every first-time bare `entire configure` run opts the user into telemetry (`settings.Telemetry = true`) without ever asking, even though this flow is explicitly framed as interactive onboarding. Consider passing telemetry consent through the onboarding form (or excluding it from the `Yes` auto-answer) so the same care given to Vercel/history import applies to telemetry.

```text
Save configuration
```

```text
Save configuration
● Save — push to main
○ Save — push to a new branch, review before it lands
○ Cancel
```

- Mirror-only changes remain local.
- Agent changes offer commit/push actions.
- Protected branches disable the direct-push destination.
- Dirty worktrees fall back to local save.
- Cancel exits without applying changes.
- Reverting selections to their original state hides Save again.

`configureGitHubAdmin` (`configure_onboarding.go:312-322`) folds every failure mode — `gh` not installed, `gh` not authenticated, network error, rate limit — into a single generic error. Here, `adminErr != nil` is treated identically to `!admin`, so a repo admin who simply lacks a working `gh` CLI locally is told "An admin needs to install the GitHub app first... send them this link" and the flow hard-exits via `NewSilentError`, even though they could complete the install themselves. The codebase already has the correct pattern for this exact dependency elsewhere (`setup_github.go`'s `ghAvailable`/`ghAuthenticated` checks with distinct, actionable messages) — this path should distinguish "check failed" from "check returned false" instead of blocking with misleading guidance.

`ensureConfigureLogin` sends the login bearer via `deps.fetchProfile(ctx, target.coreURL, target.token)` without ever calling `api.RequireSecureURL(target.coreURL)` first. Every other call site that resolves a target through `resolveAuthStatusTarget` (`auth.go`, `logout.go`, `api_cmd.go`, `repo_mirror_create_wizard.go`, `login.go`) guards the bearer with this check before sending it; this new path (both here and the second call at line 285) skips it, so a misconfigured/downgraded `coreURL` (e.g. plain HTTP) would leak the token where the rest of the codebase treats that as unacceptable.
